sections.COMMENTS:
This Composite Source straddles the marine and land area on the central portion of western Calabria, including the offshore S. Eufemia Basin and the inland S. Eufemia Plain, near the towns of Vibo Valentia (to the south) and Lametia Terme (to the north). This source is a low-angle, SE-dipping, fault located in the southwestern sector of the extensional axis that runs along the southern Apennines.
Historical catalogues (Boschi et al., 2000; Gruppo di Lavoro CPTI, 2004; Guidoboni et al., 2007) show a remarkable concentration of damaging earthquakes in the the area. In particular, this region has been struck by the 8 September 1905 Calabria earthquake (Mw ca. 7.0). The region was also affected by large earthquakes on 27 March 1638 (Mw 7.0, Calabria Centrale), 5 November 1659 (Mw 6.5, Calabria Centrale), 5 and 28 February 1783 (both Mw 7.0, Calabria).
Although the 8 September 1905 was catastrophic for this region (it also included a modest tsunami), this event remains relatively poorly documented, which led to uncertain magnitude estimates, particularly diverging among each other, and dubious epicentral location(s), most of them offshore. There is an ample literature concerning the event, Mw estimates and epicentral locations, most of them difficult to reconcile with each other and complex to be associated with known faults.
Recent offshore geophysical data by Loreto et al. (2013) helped to identify through a low-angle, SE-dipping normal fault, striking NE-SW, which these authors defined S. Eufemia Fault. This fault is associated to brittle features that ruptured the shallow deposits and the seabed, and has a regional extent. The S. Eufemia Fault is apparently the only active one in the S. Eufemia basin and seems to be prevailing one in shaping the basin and possibly a part of its on-land counterpart.
The S. Eufemia Fault also seems to be compatible with the 1905 earthquake based on fault size, seabed rupture compatible with the occurrence of the recorded tsunami, location in agreement with the distribution of the maximum damage area, and geometry compatible with the regional seismotectonic setting of the Calabrian back-arc.
A large portion of this source has been associated with the 1905 earthquake. For an in-depth analysis of seismogenic processes in this region, the reader may refer to the relevant individual source in this Database.
The strike of this Source was based on the model derived from geological and geophysical data by Loreto et al. (2013), like the dip, and the rake, indicative of almost pure normal faulting, based on geological data. The minimum and maximum depth were based on geological data and modeling by Loreto et al. (2013). The slip rate was inferred from regional geodynamic constraints data.
